title: Processes, workers and running in cluster mode

videos.script:
Every Node program you have run so far was one process, with one thread running your JavaScript. That is the right shape for almost every server. This lesson is about the two things it cannot do on its own.

{{stop}} First, stopping. A server is stopped at every deploy, with a signal called SIGTERM. You will make the links service finish the requests it has open before it exits, instead of dropping them.

{{child}} Then other programs. Node can start any program on the machine and read what it prints. There is a safe way to pass it arguments, and a way that lets a file name decide what runs.

{{threads}} Then more processors. A worker thread runs a slow calculation beside the main thread, so the server keeps answering. A pool keeps a few of them ready. And cluster runs the whole server four times, one copy per processor.

{{state}} That last one breaks the links service, and you will watch it happen: a link that exists on one copy and not on the others.

{{managers}} And at the end, the program that keeps a service running on a real server.
